description: The Great Robo-dini does a magic trick, but Duck finds the secret: it is a magnet! What sticks to a magnet? Paper clips do. Wood, plastic, paper and even a shiny foil ball do not.

youtube.title: Magnet Magic! 🧲 What Sticks to a Magnet? Science for Kids | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
The Great Robo-dini waves his magic wand and the paper clips jump! Is it magic? Duck finds the secret: it is a magnet. We test what sticks (paper clips and a jar lid) and what does not (wood, plastic, a crayon, paper and even a shiny foil ball). Magnets pull iron and steel, not every metal. Then the paper clips dance on a paper plate!

Try it at home with a grown-up: one big magnet only, a few paper clips, a paper plate, a wooden spoon, a plastic toy and a foil ball. Never use tiny magnets or magnet balls, and never put a magnet in your mouth. A grown-up counts the paper clips back into the box.

Made for kids. Toy Box Friends: 3D learning videos for preschool.

do.text: Now, three paper clips and my magic wand.
Say the magic word with me!
Banana works too! So it is not magic!
You found my secret. It is a magnet!
A magnet can pull. It pulls the paper clips.
Be a magnet! Pull, pull, pull!
What sticks to a magnet? Let's test!
Sticks goes here. No stick goes there.
A paper clip. Sticks, or no stick?
Paper clips are made of steel. Magnets pull steel!
A jar lid. Sticks, or no stick?
A wooden block. Sticks, or no stick?
A plastic ball. Sticks, or no stick?
A crayon. Sticks, or no stick?
A piece of paper. Sticks, or no stick?
Now, a shiny foil ball. It is metal!
Metal. Shiny. Sticks, or no stick?
Magnets pull iron and steel. Not every metal!
One more trick. A paper plate.
The magnet goes under the plate.
The clips dance! A magnet can pull through paper.
Do it at home, with a grown-up!
Use one big magnet. Never put magnets in your mouth.
Magnet quiz! One. A paper clip. Sticks, or no stick?
Two. A wooden block. Sticks, or no stick?
Three. The shiny foil ball. Sticks, or no stick?
No stick! Not every metal sticks.
Four. Can a magnet pull through paper?
Yes! The clips danced on the plate.
My last secret. A compass has a tiny magnet.
Duck, you are the scientist now!
Stick, click! No-go, slow! Magnets pull iron and steel!
